clue.text: Legal charges?

parts.note: the question mark hints that the charges are not fees paid to lawyers but the formal allegations brought against someone in court

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' first suggests lawyers' bills; the answer is charges in the other sense, things a defendant is accused of.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal accusations laid in court are called charges, so legal charges are exactly these allegations.

clue.text: Duck in Greek island sounds like a dove!

indicators.note: the word in tells us the duck is placed inside the name of the island

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone describes a duck on a Greek island making a noise like a dove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds like' is not a homophone signal here but the definition: a verb meaning makes a dove's noise. A duck (O) goes in COS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doves and pigeons make a soft murmuring call, so a creature that coos is making a dove's sound.

clue.text: There's no point in advising economy

definitions.meaning: something pointless, futile, serving no purpose
read as two words, an instruction to consume less, to be frugal

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into two words, a piece of advice to cut back; 'in' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: When there is no point to something it is futile, of no value at all.

clue.text: Con a diligent worker -single

parts.note: the ant is proverbially industrious, the diligent worker of the insect world
I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hard-working employee is dismissed as a con, and unmarried too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' is the opposite of pro: against, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Con as in pros and cons means opposed, the same as being against something.

clue.text: He speaks in tone that relaxes initially

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word relaxes

explanation.surface: A man talks in a soothing tone that helps listeners relax.
explanation.walkthrough: IN and TONE are given as they stand, then R from the start of 'relaxes'; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One who chants or recites in a level musical voice is a person who speaks in that way.

clue.text: The day-centre

parts.note: not a care facility but the middle point of the day, twelve o'clock

explanation.walkthrough: A day centre is a place offering daytime care; read literally it is the centre of the day, midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, twelve o'clock, sits at the very middle of the daylight hours.

clue.text: An artist whose output is not large

definitions.text: An artist whose output is not large

parts.words: An artist whose output is not large
parts.note: a painter whose works are tiny, not one who produces few pictures

explanation.walkthrough: 'output is not large' suggests an unproductive artist; it means each picture is small.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter of tiny portraits and pictures produces small-scale works by definition.

clue.text: The planting of trees in front of official premises

parts.note: fore means at or towards the front
a station is a building used as a base, such as a police station

explanation.surface: Trees are planted in front of a government building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link joining FORE and STATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Afforestation, the establishing of woodland, is the same as putting saplings into the ground.

clue.text: Cheap drink once fashionable with women

definitions.note: the definition describes a garment by its history rather than naming it, a hooped petticoat worn by women in Tudor times

parts.note: a farthing was a coin worth a quarter of an old British penny, a byword for something cheap
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A cheap drink that was once popular with women.
explanation.walkthrough: A FARTHING was a pre-1961 British coin worth a quarter of a penny. The definition describes the answer, a hooped Tudor petticoat, rather than giving a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: This hooped frame worn under skirts was a fashion item for women in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Amour" stands for ruin for this fortune teller

indicators.note: to ruin something is to wreck it, so the letters of the words before are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Love leads to ruin, according to a soothsayer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of AMOUR and STANDS are rearranged; 'for' links fodder and indicator and 'for' again links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth-century French seer famous for his prophecies is the archetypal teller of fortunes.

clue.text: The sportsman may well get ahead

definitions.text: The sportsman may well get ahead

parts.words: The sportsman may well get ahead
parts.note: a hunter of stags hopes to bag a trophy head; the answer is also a hat worn on the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'get ahead' sounds like succeeding; it means getting a stag's head as a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hunts red deer on foot is a sportsman who takes stags and their antlered heads.

clue.text: Arguments said to be mutinous

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Arguments said to be mutinous' (4) gives no parse for IDAS as held; the answer or clue appears misread and no source resolves it.

clue.text: Record notice

definitions.meaning: to observe or take heed of

explanation.definitionFit: To jot something down is to make a written memo; to observe is to take heed of a thing.

clue.text: Having sent in wrong key is really serious

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is one of the musical keys, A to G

explanation.surface: Someone who entered the wrong key finds the situation grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges SENT IN to INTENS, then E is added; 'Having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extreme in degree or deeply earnest is grave and fierce.

clue.text: A consumer of some taste — a terse fellow

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, the letters running inside them

explanation.surface: Someone with refined taste is also a man of few words.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'tastE A TERse'; 'of' and 'fellow' are padding links.
explanation.definitionFit: One who eats food is a consumer of it.

clue.text: A teller of stories after following soldiers

indicators.note: following says the word for after comes behind the soldiers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers of the British Army
later means afterwards

explanation.surface: A storyteller arrives after the troops have passed.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: One who recounts or narrates tales is a storyteller.

clue.text: Come to a stretch of water

definitions.meaning: to arrive at, get as far as
a straight section of a river between bends

explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a place is to get there; a river section between bends has the same name.

clue.text: Give way with little hesitation — it's wiser!

parts.note: to sag is to droop or give way under weight
er is the short sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Yielding after a brief pause is the more sensible course.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word for wise or sagacious, more full of wisdom.

clue.text: The expedition set off

definitions.meaning: to trigger, as one sets off an alarm

explanation.definitionFit: A journey or outing is an excursion; to trigger an alarm or mechanism is to activate it.

clue.text: Deny oneself unflinchingly

definitions.meaning: firmly, without wavering, as in standing firm

explanation.definitionFit: To go without food is to abstain; holding firm without wavering is standing steadfastly.

clue.text: Respond and create endless agitation

indicators.note: agitation stirs and shakes the letters of the trimmed word into a new order
endless means the final letter of the word create is cut off

explanation.surface: Respond to something and stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims CREATE to CREAT, and 'agitation' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer or behave in response to something is to reply to it.

clue.text: Use pair bonding to give lift

indicators.note: bonding joins the two words into one and recombines their letters in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple is told to stick together to boost morale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bonding' fuses USE and PAIR into one set of letters; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to elevate it upward.

clue.text: Person travelling to ancient city first

parts.note: taken as written
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
first written as 1ST, which reads as IST with the figure one as the letter I

explanation.surface: A traveller visits an ancient city before anywhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' abbreviates to 1st, and the numeral 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A holidaymaker or sightseer is someone travelling for pleasure.

clue.text: Gun turned on a rebel leader as ordered

indicators.note: turned means the name of the gun is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of the word rebel

explanation.surface: A rebel chief has a gun pointed at him on command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses LUGER to REGUL; then A and R, the first letter of 'rebel'. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Done according to rule and pattern, things that are orderly follow a set system.

clue.text: One should require no additional luggage

definitions.text: One should require no additional luggage

parts.words: One should require no additional luggage
parts.note: a bag big enough to take everything, so no other case is needed

explanation.walkthrough: The bag's name read as two words says it takes everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A large capacious travel bag carries everything, hence its name.

clue.text: Small type-that's material

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ilk means kind or sort

explanation.surface: Tiny print is what makes up the fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine fabric spun by silkworms is a fabric, a material.

clue.text: The knot tier shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the word is written from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a rank is a level or tier

explanation.surface: The person who tied the knot is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tier' looks like one who ties; it is a level, RANK, and 'shown up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnarl in wood or a tree is a hard knob, a knot.

clue.text: Pop in a steamer and they'll be health-giving

indicators.note: in tells us father goes inside the abbreviation for the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad boards a steamship and expects the trip to do him good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' tempts as a burst or a fizzy drink; here it is father. 'a steamer' is any steamship, abbreviated as ships' names are prefixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mineral-spring resorts are visited for their health benefits.

clue.text: Quiet English river, quite unpolluted

parts.note: p, piano, means quietly in music
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A calm English river is clean.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical mark piano, softly; the Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of contamination is clean and unadulterated.

clue.text: Ridiculous pose struck by South Americans

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests something absurd, so the letters of the word beside it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some South Americans strike an absurd pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struck' is minting: the coin is struck, as currency, in several South American countries.
explanation.definitionFit: This coin is the currency minted in several Latin American countries such as Chile and Argentina.

clue.text: See printers working out schemes

indicators.note: working out suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Look at printers figuring out plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' rearranges SEE PRINTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventures or undertakings are projects or plans.

clue.text: A suggestion of professional standing

parts.note: pro is short for professional
position means status or standing

explanation.surface: A proposal comes from someone of professional status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal or offer put forward is a suggestion.
